evidence: The 9e51cb1 diff deletes three divergent MockTransport copies: the notifications.rs copy had MockState { closed } only, discarded sends via `let _ = command`, and its read() had no closed guard, exactly as the reviewer said. The union now lives once in tests/support/mod.rs.
guidance_note: When a PR moves some test helpers into tests/support, move every per-file test double at the same time instead of leaving copies in each test binary.

evidence: Before 9e51cb1, detach() was `self.transport.send(...).map_err(TmuxError::Send)` and set no state, while execute/consume_greeting closed on failure at four hand-written sites. Routing every send and read through send_or_close/read_or_close fixes the bug and removes the duplication. But the helper ignored the documented 'Closed is terminal' invariant, which F6/F7 then caught.
guidance_note: When a fix sends a new caller (detach, documented as callable from any state) through a shared state-transition helper, check the helper against every pre-state that caller can arrive in, including terminal Closed.

evidence: The round-0 hunk shows new() spelling out all six fields with state Ready, and connect() repeating the same literal with Connecting. In 9e51cb1 both go through with_state(transport, state), as the reviewer proposed.
guidance_note: When adding a second constructor, factor the shared field initialization into one private builder before writing the second struct literal.

evidence: `use crate::client::ConnectionState` in error.rs does depend on mod.rs's re-export rather than on the sibling module that defines the type. Calling it a 'real two-way coupling' overstates a one-line import path in Rust; nothing breaks today. The one-line change to `super::connection_state::ConnectionState` in 9e51cb1 is cheap and correct.

The agent agreed that pane_output/notifications are unbounded VecDeques. It deferred the fix to ticket tmux-buffering-09s because every remedy changes the public contract (the documented buffer-not-drop promise and the drain_* API). It later settled the design on that ticket (require sinks at construction, delete the buffers), which rewrites 15 tests. That is a defensible scope deferral with the issue tracked, not a dismissal.
guidance_note: When a module promises 'buffered, not dropped' for a path its own docs call high-volume, decide the retention bound or sink-at-construction design before publishing that promise.

evidence: 9e51cb1 changed detach() to `self.send_or_close(&CommandLine::detach())`, and send_or_close unconditionally assigns Closed { TransportError }. So close() followed by detach() now rewrites Disposed, where before the fix detach set no state at all. The agent admits 'I introduced it last round'. Its absorbing ConnectionState::closed() in 5307896 covers all four assignment sites rather than just this call path.
guidance_note: When centralizing 'transport failure closes the connection', also centralize the documented 'Closed is terminal' rule on the state type, and add a detach-after-close test in the same commit.

evidence: This is the same defect as F6 (close() then detach() clobbers Disposed with TransportError through 9e51cb1's send_or_close), raised as a second thread in the same round. It was fixed by the same 5307896 closed() transition, and the agent cross-referenced the two threads.
guidance_note: When centralizing 'transport failure closes the connection', also centralize the documented 'Closed is terminal' rule on the state type, and add a detach-after-close test in the same commit.

evidence: The flag is a false positive. 5307896 changed only connection_state.rs, the closed() call sites, and a test. The reconnect() doc quoting DESIGN.md §3.3 ('re-enters Connecting') and the `self.state = Reconnecting { attempt }` code were both in the PR from round 0. The mismatch is real. The reviewer offered two remedies (change the code or change the doc), and the agent took the doc-side one with sound reasoning: Reconnecting carries attempt and the gate is Ready-only.
guidance_note: When a doc comment quotes a design document verbatim, check that the code takes every state transition the quote names before committing it.

evidence: The flag is a false positive. The never-cleared `if self.fail_next_send { return Err(...) }` is byte-for-byte the logic of the pre-review client.rs mock, which 9e51cb1 only relocated into tests/support (5307896 does not touch it). The flag's name does promise one-shot behavior the code did not keep. The fix plus a test that the second detach succeeds is proportionate.
guidance_note: When promoting a test double to a shared harness, check that each field's name matches its behavior, since every test binary inherits the contract.

narrative: Round 0 raised five findings. The agent fixed four in 9e51cb1 and deferred the unbounded-buffer one (F5) to a ticket. Its F2 fix routed detach() through a new send_or_close helper that ignored the terminal-Closed invariant, and round 1 reported the resulting detach-after-close regression twice (F6, F7). Those were fixed with an absorbing ConnectionState::closed(). Round 2's findings (F8 doc/design mismatch, F9 one-shot flag) sit on pre-review or merely relocated code. Round 3 hit the review cap and reviewed nothing, so 57b3126 shipped unreviewed.
guidance_observations: The agent's single-owner refactor for F2 was the right shape but centralized one invariant while leaving the neighbouring one (Closed is terminal) unowned; a test for every documented pre-state of the newly routed caller would have caught it before round 1.
Round 2 also reported an out-of-diff comment drift in transport/mod.rs ('a later ticket') that has no thread and no recorded disposition.
The final fix commit 57b3126, which edited DESIGN.md, merged with no review because the round cap was reached; the agent flagged this openly in the thread.

evidence: `format!("{name}:{what}:{format}")` over arbitrary &str does shift tmux's field boundaries when name contains ':'. The agent replaced name with a colon-rejecting SubscriptionName newtype and what with a closed SubscriptionScope enum. It checked against live tmux that only the first two colons split, so format stays unrestricted and a test pins that.
guidance_note: When building one delimiter-joined argument that the server splits, type each caller-supplied field so the delimiter cannot be represented, and check which fields the server actually splits.

evidence: The hunk shows `unsubscribe` passing a raw &str name to `-B`, and tmux dispatches -B on whether the argument contains a colon, so a colon flips the remove into a subscribe. Taking &SubscriptionName, the same type as the F1 fix, makes that argument impossible to construct.
guidance_note: When building one delimiter-joined argument that the server splits, type each caller-supplied field so the delimiter cannot be represented, and check which fields the server actually splits.

evidence: `flags.join(",")` over &[&str] lets an embedded comma or a leading '!' change which flags tmux sees. The agent adopted the closed ClientFlag enum the reviewer suggested, deleted the redundant NO_OUTPUT_FLAG const, and built -f's argument in one join_flags helper.
guidance_note: When building one delimiter-joined argument that the server splits, type each caller-supplied field so the delimiter cannot be represented, and check which fields the server actually splits.

narrative: All three round-0 findings were the same delimiter-injection gap across subscribe, unsubscribe and set/clear_flags. One commit (f5de9c5) fixed them by making the delimiters unrepresentable in types, and round 1 approved with no findings. The agent verified tmux's actual colon-splitting behavior live before deciding which field to leave unrestricted.
guidance_observations: All three findings share one root, raw &str fields joined into a server-split argument; an accept/reject shape table for each joined argument before writing the functions would have removed the round.

evidence: The agent instrumented the window and found 0 buffered pane-output entries in 6/6 runs, so 'very likely to occur' is overstated. But lifecycle.bin shows that pre-flag %output can arrive, so the assertion depended on a race. The agent also noted the assertion did not separate pre-flag from post-flag output. Draining right after set_no_output scopes the assertion correctly.
guidance_note: When asserting that a flag suppresses a stream, drain the stream when the flag takes effect, so the assertion covers only output that arrived after it.

evidence: `let _ = client.execute(&line("list-sessions", NO_ARGS));` discards the error, so a dead transport surfaces only as the generic 'expected a WindowAdd notification' failure. It was replaced with an .expect() that names the poll and the connection.
guidance_note: In tests, never discard a Result with `let _ =` on a call that talks to the system under test; use expect with a message naming the cause.

narrative: Round 0 raised two test-quality findings in the live conformance test: a race-dependent pane-output assertion and a swallowed poll error. dbd9b14 fixed both, and round 1 approved. The agent tried to reproduce the race before accepting, and accepted on the strength of the mechanism rather than the repro.

evidence: In `if let Some(mut child) = lock(&self.child).take() { kill; wait }` the MutexGuard temporary lives through the whole then-block, in Rust 2024 as well, so a racing KillHandle::kill() blocks until close()'s wait() returns, against its doc. The thread has no reply and is unresolved, but it is marked outdated and the PR merged; the packet does not show whether a later commit fixed the line silently.
guidance_note: When a lock guards a slot that is taken and then followed by a blocking call, bind the taken value in its own statement so the guard drops before the blocking call.

narrative: The single round raised one real concurrency finding: the if-let scrutinee holds the ChildSlot mutex across kill() and the blocking wait(). The thread got no reply and was never resolved, yet the PR merged a day later. The finding is marked outdated, so the line changed, but the packet does not show whether the change addressed it.
guidance_observations: A CHANGES_REQUESTED finding merged with no reply and no resolution, breaking the address-pr-reviews contract; every thread needs a recorded disposition before merge.
